What you're actually choosing

An archetype is three decisions in one:

  • Attribute ranges. Where you start and how high each stat can go. A Magician's Standing Tackle caps at 80; a Boss reaches 99. That gap never closes, no matter how you spend points.
  • Two perks. Permanent, archetype-specific, and they amplify habits rather than creating them. Cut Back Specialist does nothing for a player who cuts inside and shoots every time.
  • Three specializations. Unlocked by hitting specific attribute ratings — the numbers shown on each card above. They re-point a build significantly: Thief and Driver are the same Recycler base aimed at two different jobs.

How to pick without regretting it

  1. Fill your club's gap, not your fantasy. A squad with three Magicians and no Recycler loses to organised opponents. The unglamorous archetypes win matches.
  2. Match how you already play. If you never reach the byline, Spark's cut-back perk is wasted on you.
  3. Check the specialization requirements before you commit. They're listed on every card above. Some sit within two points of the archetype's own ceiling, meaning you must max that attribute almost exactly to qualify.

Frequently asked questions

How many archetypes are in Pro Clubs?

Thirteen — 2 keeper, 4 defender, 4 midfielder and 3 forward.

Which archetype is best?

There isn't one. They're balanced against each other, not ranked. The strongest pick is whichever fills a hole in your club's shape.

Can I change archetype later?

Yes, but it resets the progression tied to that archetype — worth getting roughly right first.

Perks, specializations and unlock requirements from the Pro Clubs Lobby catalog.






What you're actually choosing

An archetype is three decisions in one:

 * Attribute ranges. Where you start and how high each stat can go. A Magician's Standing Tackle caps at 80; a Boss reaches 99. That gap never closes, no matter how you spend points.
 * Two perks. Permanent, archetype-specific, and they amplify habits rather than creating them. Cut Back Specialist does nothing for a player who cuts inside and shoots every time.
 * Three specializations. Unlocked by hitting specific attribute ratings — the numbers shown on each card above. They re-point a build significantly: Thief and Driver are the same Recycler base aimed at two different jobs.


How to pick without regretting it

 1. Fill your club's gap, not your fantasy. A squad with three Magicians and no Recycler loses to organised opponents. The unglamorous archetypes win matches.
 2. Match how you already play. If you never reach the byline, Spark's cut-back perk is wasted on you.
 3. Check the specialization requirements before you commit. They're listed on every card above. Some sit within two points of the archetype's own ceiling, meaning you must max that attribute almost exactly to qualify.


Frequently asked questions


How many archetypes are in Pro Clubs?

Thirteen — 2 keeper, 4 defender, 4 midfielder and 3 forward.


Which archetype is best?

There isn't one. They're balanced against each other, not ranked. The strongest pick is whichever fills a hole in your club's shape.


Can I change archetype later?

Yes, but it resets the progression tied to that archetype — worth getting roughly right first.

No. Every archetype trades a high ceiling in one area for a low one elsewhere. What matters is whether its strengths match the role you actually play.

posts.title: Which EA FC Pro Clubs Archetype Should You Play?
posts.html:
Four questions, no sign-up, answers update as you click:

Which archetype should you play?

Four questions, scored against every archetype's real attribute ceilings — not opinion.

1 · Where do you want to play?
2 · What kind of keeper?
2 · What do you want to be best at?
3 · And solid at?
4 · What can you live without?

Answer above and your best-fit archetypes appear here.

Weighting: best × 3, solid × 1.5, live-without × −0.5, applied to each archetype's category ceiling normalised across the outfield pool.

How it decides

No hand-written recommendations. Each outfield archetype has a ceiling in six attribute categories, taken from the Pro Clubs Lobby catalog. Those ceilings sit in different bands — every archetype has decent Ball Control, almost none have elite Defending — so each category is normalised across the pool first. Otherwise Ball Control would quietly decide every answer.

Your picks are then weighted: what you want to be best at counts triple, solid at counts one-and-a-half, and what you'll give up subtracts a little as a tiebreak. The bars show the spread across the whole pool, so a narrow win looks narrow.

If you'd rather just read it

Highest ceiling in each category:

  • Pace — Spark (97)
  • Ball Control — Maestro (98)
  • Passing — Creator (98)
  • Scoring — Finisher (99)
  • Defending — Boss (98)
  • Physical — Boss (97)

Two things the quiz can't weigh. Your club's shape matters more than your preference — a team of Magicians loses to an organised side, and the Recycler nobody wants to play is often why good clubs win. And perks amplify habits rather than creating them: Cut Back Specialist does nothing for a player who cuts inside and shoots every time.

Keepers are a different question

There are only two keeper archetypes and the choice isn't really about attributes — it's whether your defence plays a high line. Shot Stopper is built to keep the ball out and nothing else. Sweeper Keeper is comfortable receiving back passes and rushing off the line, which is an asset behind a high line and a liability behind a defence that just clears it.

Frequently asked questions

Which archetype is best in Pro Clubs?

There isn't one. Archetypes are balanced against each other rather than ranked. The strongest pick is the one filling a gap in your club.

Can I change archetype later?

Yes, though it resets the progression tied to that archetype.

Does this account for playstyles?

Not yet — it scores attribute ceilings only. Signature playstyles and the PlayStyle+ options attached to each specialization are a separate layer on top of the archetype choice.

posts.title: Explosive, Lengthy or Controlled: How AcceleRATE Works in Pro Clubs
posts.html:
Set your height and drag the two sliders — the acceleration type updates live, with the exact rule that decided it:

AcceleRATE calculator

Height, Agility and Strength decide how your pro accelerates. Nothing else — not Pace.

Thresholds unverified for FC 26. EA has never published them; these are community-documented values that have held since FIFA 23. The height and attribute limits below are from the Pro Clubs Lobby catalog. Spot-check in-game before trusting exact boundaries.

Archetype

—

Reachable by this archetype

Height and attribute limits from the Pro Clubs Lobby catalog. Threshold rules are community-sourced.

The one thing to understand

It's the gap that matters, not the raw numbers. Pushing Agility to 99 does nothing if you also pushed Strength to 95. Players chasing Explosive routinely ruin it by levelling Strength "because it seemed useful".

Explosive wants you short, with Agility well clear of Strength. Lengthy wants you tall, with Strength well clear of Agility. Controlled is the fallback when neither gap is wide enough — which is where most players land by accident.

Explosive players hit top speed over the first few yards and fade. Lengthy players start slowly and keep accelerating past the point everyone else has topped out. There are also half-steps — Mostly and Controlled variants — that relax the height limit and the required gap.

Which archetypes can reach which type

Your archetype constrains height and caps both attributes, so not every type is available to every archetype. Computed from the Pro Clubs Lobby catalog's own ranges:

ArchetypeHeightAgilityStrengthBest ExplosiveBest Lengthy
Shot Stopper183–201cm50–9050–96—Lengthy
Sweeper Keeper178–198cm65–9065–96Mostly ExplosiveLengthy
Progressor178–196cm70–9070–96Mostly ExplosiveLengthy
Boss180–196cm65–9075–99Mostly ExplosiveLengthy
Engine168–188cm70–9265–96ExplosiveLengthy
Marauder168–188cm70–9560–96ExplosiveLengthy
Recycler173–193cm70–9275–96Mostly ExplosiveLengthy
Maestro163–188cm72–9965–92ExplosiveLengthy
Creator163–188cm72–9965–92ExplosiveLengthy
Spark163–188cm75–9965–90ExplosiveMostly Lengthy
Magician163–188cm72–9965–90ExplosiveMostly Lengthy
Finisher165–191cm72–9970–92ExplosiveLengthy
Target178–196cm70–9275–99Mostly ExplosiveLengthy

7 of the 13 can reach full Explosive — Engine, Marauder, Maestro, Creator, Spark, Magician and Finisher — all sharing a low minimum height with a high Agility ceiling. The 6 that cannot (Shot Stopper, Sweeper Keeper, Progressor, Boss, Recycler and Target) are blocked by height alone: their shortest legal build is still taller than the Explosive limit.

Full Lengthy is easier — only Spark and Magician cannot reach it, clearing the height bar but keeping a Strength ceiling too close to their Agility floor to open a 20-point gap. Every archetype can reach at least the Controlled Lengthy half-step.

Getting the type you want

  1. Set height first. It's the only input you can't change later, and it gates everything — above the Explosive height limit, you can never be Explosive regardless of attributes.
  2. Then protect the gap. Chasing Explosive means treating Strength as something to leave alone.
  3. Re-check after every upgrade. One point in the wrong attribute can flip you from Explosive to Mostly Explosive, silently.

Frequently asked questions

Does Pace affect AcceleRATE?

No. Acceleration and Sprint Speed change how fast you end up going; they play no part in which profile you get. Only height, Agility and Strength do.

Is Explosive better than Lengthy?

Neither. Explosive wins the first few yards, suiting wingers and tight spaces. Lengthy wins longer runs, suiting centre-backs and strikers running in behind.

Can I change my acceleration type later?

The attribute half, yes — the Agility/Strength gap moves as you spend points. Height is fixed at creation, so if height rules a type out, it's out permanently.
